reviewType: Focused code and real PostgreSQL regression review of the new public OTP, engagement and notification boundaries
status: No remaining concrete blocker identified within the reviewed scope

closedFindings.finding: Dedicated managed-resource publication lacked publication notification fanout
closedFindings.resolution: Added a separate durable event linked to immutable resource publication history. Public current version, matching reviewed metadata, independent approval, current publisher/reviewer permission, locale, clean scan and distribution rights are checked before fanout and again at actual dispatch. Private/authenticated documents are never broadcast.

closedFindings.finding: The administrator directory omitted phone and placeholder flags needed for safe phone-only account projection
closedFindings.resolution: The directory selects the required fields, hides internal placeholder addresses, exposes verified phone identity and supports normalized Iranian/international phone search without expanding punctuation-only searches. Current administrative access remains mandatory.

closedFindings.finding: Generic managed-resource metadata authorization allowed engagement reads after its strict public page became unavailable
closedFindings.resolution: Engagement now uses the existing strict resource-page resolver and reuses its caller transaction. Previously approved comments are suppressed after scan or distribution rights withdrawal; writes to the unavailable document also fail closed.

closedFindings.finding: The expanded content topic allowed timed notice fanout without the existing public visibility window check
closedFindings.resolution: Reuse publicNoticePublicationVisible at current-event authorization. Disabled or expired notices do not enqueue; valid future notices retain a durable event and are skipped until their public start without blocking other ready events. Final delivery rechecks the same visibility and locale. Content consent remains required.

reviewedControls: Customer OTP cannot authenticate staff or inactive accounts; phone redemption is serialized, expiry and attempt budgets persist, and repeated concurrent redemption creates one session.
OTP and channel proofs are not returned as plaintext API results or included in cost reports; outbox endpoints and proof payloads are encrypted.
Pending/rejected comments do not appear publicly; approval requires a different authorized moderator, current locale, MFA and expected record version.
Role-routed request and signed-connector alerts contain a minimal reference and protected link; current recipient permissions are checked again before dispatch.
Publication notifications preserve explicit topic and channel consent, current binding, locale, quiet hours and digest behavior. Unknown costs remain unknown.
AI assistance rechecks current role/locale after generation and never publishes, sends customer responses or approves content automatically.

The additive resource event relation is covered by dynamic runtime grants and backup relation inventory. Existing publication history continues to block unreviewed author erasure; no customer contact text is copied into event receipts.
documentedBoundaries: Comments are flat; nested replies and independent outbound moderation alerts are not implemented.
External telephone calls require a real PBX/connector adapter; manual CRM notes do not synthesize connector events.
A provider acceptance is not recipient delivery or reading. No real external messages were sent in this validation.
Visit metrics are browser-window approximations, not unique-person or bot-free counts.
Live domain DNS, email delivery reputation and paid-provider credentials require deployment-specific acceptance.
This focused review is not a complete penetration test or a claim that all possible vulnerabilities are absent.
